newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan import prices on slight rising trend-govt.
newsitem.headline: Japan import prices on slight rising trend-govt.

text.p: Japan's import prices are on a slight rising trend but overall prices are stable, an official of the Management and Coordination Agency said on Friday.
"Import prices are somewhat on a rising trend, though the rise is slight," the official said, adding that the weaker yen had contributed to the price rise.
But he said overall prices were stable, adding that the rise in import prices was contributing only about 0.05 percent to the overall figure.

He also said that consumer prices from January to March had been flat in year-on-year terms, although April consumer prices for the Tokyo area rose 1.2 percent. The rise was the highest since March 1994 and followed an increase in the sales tax to five percent from three percent on April 1.
"In 1995 and 1996 prices have been falling, and there hasn't been a rise of over one percent," the official said.
An official with the Economic Planning Agency said the rise in the April figures for Tokyo were in line with the agency's forecast effect of the sales tax rise.
Officials said, however, that they could not exactly say how much of the 1.2 percent year-on-year rise in April was due to the sales tax increase.
